title: Commands with Pronouns
description: Give commands with objects: Donne-le-moi! (Give it to me!), Regarde-moi! (Look at me!), Ne le fais pas! (Don't do it!)
can_do: Give commands with object pronouns (Give it to me!)
Use pronouns with affirmative and negative commands
Form complex commands like 'Don't do it!' or 'Look at me!'
Say some or how many with {en}: {j'en veux}, {j'en ai trois}.

concepts.definition: In positive commands, pronouns attach to the verb with hyphens
concepts.example: {Donne-le!} (Give it!), {Regarde-moi!} (Look at me!), {Écoute-le!} (Listen to him!), {Regarde-moi et fais attention!} (Look at me and pay attention!), {Amuse-toi bien!} (Have fun!), {Dépêche-toi, habille-toi!} (Hurry up, get dressed!)

concepts.definition: In negative commands, pronouns go BEFORE the verb (normal position)
concepts.example: {Ne le fais pas!} (Don't do it!), {Ne me regarde pas!} (Don't look at me!)

concepts.definition: Object pronouns: le/la/les come first, then moi/toi
concepts.example: {Donne-le-moi!} (Give it to me! - le before moi), {Montre-la-moi!} (Show it to me!)

concepts.definition: {en} stands for something you already named with {du}, {de la}, {de l'}, {des} or a number. In a statement it goes before the verb. In a positive command it goes after the verb, with a hyphen, like the other pronouns.
concepts.example: {Tu veux du café ? Oui, j'en veux.} (Do you want some coffee? Yes, I want some.), {Prends-en !} (Take some!)

items.hint: Ne + le + fais + pas (pronoun BEFORE verb in negative)

mistakes.feedback: In negative commands, pronoun goes BEFORE: Ne le fais pas!

items.situation: Command: 'Give it to me!' (informal, it = le)
A friend asks {Tu veux du café ?} Say yes, you want some. Use {en}.
A friend asks {Tu as des livres ?} Say yes, you have three. Use {en}.
items.hint: {en} before the verb, the number at the end

mistakes.feedback: Keep {en} before the verb, even with a number: {j'en ai trois}.

items.situation: Offer a friend some of your bread. Say “Take some!” with {en}.
items.hint: Like {donne-le}: the pronoun goes after the verb, with a hyphen

mistakes.feedback: In a positive command, {en} goes after the verb: {prends-en}.
